messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden 503 spike for hosted inference (us-west-2). error rate ~38% over last 6m, top affected customer: acme-corp. sample request ids: rq_3f4a, rq_3f4b. routing layer seeing upstream worker exits.
ryan_oncall: I'm on it, pulling logs now.
jamie_cs: CS: acme reports 50% of requests failing, they see timeouts then 503. They're on our hosted-tier, model: gptx-13b-open, high qps.
sarah_infra: node logs show repeated OOM kills + container restarts on pool hosted-gpu-01. kernel message: 'Tasks killed as a result of limit of cgroup.memory.limit_in_bytes'. Likely cgroup OOM (not just CUDA OOM). snippet: 
```
Mar 01 09:12:21 host kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 21456 (infer_runner) score 925 or sacrifice child
Mar 01 09:12:21 host kernel: Killed process 21456 (infer_runner) total-vm:75432128kB, anon-rss:73400320kB, file-rss:0kB
Mar 01 09:12:21 host systemd: infer-runner.service: Main process exited, code=killed, status=9/KILL
```
ryan_oncall: interesting — we also see segfault traces in runtime just before kill for some runs. possible memory balloon from KV prefetch + large batch windows. mike_runtime, can you confirm if recent runtime change affects prefetch behavior?
mike_runtime: yes, recent dynbatch change reduces per-request latency but increases prefetched KV size for large contexts. Telemetry shows KV cache grow to ~28GB for some requests before OOM. Also saw occasional SIGSEGV in attention kernel prior to oom on same pid.
jamie_cs: CS update: told acme to switch to a lower concurrency client and we opened a temporary ticket to reduce batch size server-side. They want ETA.
sarah_infra: immediate mitigations: 1) cordon the most impacted node (host-172.31.9.45) 2) scale up pool by 2 nodes 3) add a temporary higher cgroup mem limit for pool, 4) route acme traffic to fallback model variant (gptx-6b) until fix. Deploy-bot: can you start canary route now?
deploy-bot: started canary routing acme -> hosted-fallback-6b (10% -> 100%) and increased autoscaler min size +2 for hosted-gpu-01.
ryan_oncall: repro plan for infra/runtime: (1) reproduce with stress script: heavy-embed-job --model gptx-13b-open --batch 48 --prefetch=on --concurrency 16 (2) capture /proc/<pid>/smaps before crash (3) enable extra kv-prefetch logging and core dumps as allowed.
mike_runtime: adding extra logs: KVCache.prefetch_size, attention_alloc, and dumping last 100 lines of runtime stderr on exit. I also toggled a guard to cap prefetch to 20GB for now.
sarah_infra: ticket INC-2026 created, linked to acme support thread. ramped cgroup to 92GB on pool nodes as temporary stopgap. Watch CPU/PCIe mem pressure.
jamie_cs: customer notified: we've routed to fallback and are seeing success rate recover to 97%. They requested postmortem and ETA for permanent fix.
ryan_oncall: root-cause hypothesis: dynbatch + aggressive KV prefetch allow per-request memory ballooning that combined with a cgroup ceiling and occasional kernel-level fragmentation triggers OOM and then container restart; segfaults are likely memory corruption from kernel-ish driver or attention kernel under heavy memory pressure. Next: reproduce locally with controlled mem limit, add regression test for prefetch growth, and consider memory-accounting change in runtime.
mike_runtime: I'll revert the dynbatch heuristic for hot paths in the next patch and backport a prefetch cap to stable.
sarah_infra: follow-ups: schedule postmortem, add autoscaler policy to prefer scaling nodes rather than allowing cgroup saturation, and add an alert on rapid prefetch growth per-request.
jamie_cs: noted for customer: PM will follow up with detailed timeline.
ryan_oncall: marking incident as mitigated — rollback on dynbatch in progress, canary routing stable. Will update with postmortem link later. :white_check_mark:
